objects.description: Callable object type that forwards to the free function tag_invoke via ADL, preserving noexcept and return type. Instances serve as customization point objects (CPOs).

objects.definition: using yes_type = char;
objects.description: Alias used as a probe type (sizeof 1) in SFINAE to detect a valid tag_invoke expression.

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _unit { struct unit {}; } using _unit::unit; }
objects.description: An empty tag type representing a unit/void-like value type useful in metaprogramming where a non-void, empty type is required.
Customization point object for invoking set_value on a receiver, preferring tag_invoke if available, otherwise calling a member set_value. Provided as an inline const object named set_value.
Customization point object for invoking set_next on a receiver, preferring tag_invoke if available, otherwise calling a member set_next. Provided as an inline const object named set_next.

Customization point object for invoking set_error on a receiver. Requires nothrow and void return when tag_invoked; otherwise calls a noexcept member set_error. Provided as inline const object set_error.
Customization point object for invoking set_done on a receiver, preferring tag_invoke if available, otherwise calling a noexcept member set_done. Provided as inline const object set_done.

Customization point object type for start(). Invoking start(op) will call tag_invoke(_fn{}, op) if available, otherwise op.start(). Requires the operation’s start to be noexcept. The global instance is unifex::start.

Customization point object type for connect(). It connects a Sender to a Receiver, preferring tag_invoke(connect, S, R), otherwise falling back to member S.connect(R). When async stack injection is enabled, it wraps the returned operation in an instrumentation wrapper. The global instance is unifex::connect.

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _schedule { struct _fn { private: template <typename Scheduler> static auto impl_(Scheduler sched) noexcept(noexcept(make_sender_for<schedule>( _impl{}((Scheduler &&) sched), get_scheduler = Scheduler(sched)))) { return make_sender_for<schedule>( _impl{}((Scheduler &&) sched), get_scheduler = Scheduler(sched)); } public: template(typename Scheduler)         (requires scheduler<Scheduler>)        auto operator()(Scheduler&& sched) const noexcept(noexcept(_fn::impl_((Scheduler &&) sched))) -> decltype(_fn::impl_((Scheduler &&) sched)) { return _fn::impl_((Scheduler &&) sched); } constexpr sender operator()() const noexcept; }; } }
objects.description: Customization-point object type for schedule. It dispatches to either tag_invoke(schedule, scheduler) or a scheduler's .schedule() member, and also supports nullary form to create a sender that reschedules on the receiver's current scheduler.

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _schedule { struct _impl { private: template <typename Scheduler> static auto _select() noexcept { if constexpr (_with_tag_invoke<Scheduler>) { return meta_tag_invoke_result<_fn>{}; } else if constexpr (_with_member_schedule<Scheduler>) { return meta_quote1<_member_schedule_result_t>{}; } else { return type_always<void>{}; } } template <typename Scheduler> using _result_t = typename decltype(_impl::_select<Scheduler>())::template apply<Scheduler>; public: template(typename Scheduler)                (requires _with_tag_invoke<Scheduler>)       constexpr auto operator()(Scheduler&& s) const noexcept(is_nothrow_tag_invocable_v<_fn, Scheduler>) -> _result_t<Scheduler> { return tag_invoke(schedule, static_cast<Scheduler&&>(s)); } template(typename Scheduler)       (requires(! _with_tag_invoke<Scheduler>) AND _with_member_schedule<Scheduler>)        constexpr auto operator()(Scheduler&& s) const noexcept(noexcept(static_cast<Scheduler&&>(s).schedule())) -> _result_t<Scheduler> { return static_cast<Scheduler&&>(s).schedule(); } }; template <typename S> using _schedule_result_t = decltype(_impl{}(UNIFEX_DECLVAL(S &&))); } }
objects.description: Internal dispatcher that selects how to obtain a schedule sender from a Scheduler: via tag_invoke or via .schedule() member. Used to implement schedule CPO.

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _schedule { struct sender { template < template <typename...> class Variant, template <typename...> class Tuple> using value_types = Variant<Tuple<>>; template <template <typename...> class Variant> using error_types = Variant<std::exception_ptr>; static constexpr bool sends_done = true; static constexpr blocking_kind blocking = blocking_kind::maybe; static constexpr bool is_always_scheduler_affine = true; template(typename Receiver)        (requires receiver<Receiver>)        friend auto tag_invoke(tag_t<connect>, sender, Receiver&& r) -> connect_result_t< schedule_result_t< get_scheduler_result_t<const remove_cvref_t<Receiver>&>>, Receiver> { auto scheduler = get_scheduler(std::as_const(r)); return connect(schedule(std::move(scheduler)), (Receiver &&) r); } }; inline constexpr sender _fn::operator()() const noexcept { return {}; } } }
objects.description: A sender type returned by schedule() with no arguments. When connected, it asks the receiver for its scheduler and delegates to schedule(scheduler). Sends only completion (no value).

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _get_scheduler { struct _fn { template(typename SchedulerProvider)                         (requires tag_invocable<_fn, const SchedulerProvider&>)       auto operator()(const SchedulerProvider& context) const noexcept -> tag_invoke_result_t<_fn, const SchedulerProvider&> { static_assert(is_nothrow_tag_invocable_v<_fn, const SchedulerProvider&>); static_assert( scheduler<tag_invoke_result_t<_fn, const SchedulerProvider&>>); return tag_invoke(*this, context); } template(typename T)                              (requires(!same_as<_fn, remove_cvref_t<T>>))       constexpr kv<_fn, remove_cvref_t<T>> operator=(T&& t) const& noexcept( std::is_nothrow_constructible_v<remove_cvref_t<T>, T>) { return {*this, (T &&) t}; } }; } }
objects.description: Customization-point object for retrieving a scheduler from a scheduler provider (e.g., receiver or promise). Requires tag_invoke support by the provider. Provides assignment-style binder.

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _schedule_after { inline const struct _fn { private: template <typename TimeScheduler, typename Duration> using _schedule_after_member_result_t = decltype(UNIFEX_DECLVAL(TimeScheduler) .schedule_after(UNIFEX_DECLVAL(Duration))); template <typename TimeScheduler, typename Duration> using _result_t = typename conditional_t< tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler, Duration>, meta_tag_invoke_result<_fn>, meta_quote2<_schedule_after_member_result_t>>:: template apply<TimeScheduler, Duration>; public: template(typename TimeScheduler, typename Duration)         (requires tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler, Duration>)       constexpr auto operator()(TimeScheduler&& s, Duration&& d) const noexcept(is_nothrow_tag_invocable_v<_fn, TimeScheduler, Duration>) -> _result_t<TimeScheduler, Duration> { return tag_invoke(*this, (TimeScheduler &&) s, (Duration &&) d); } template(typename TimeScheduler, typename Duration)           (requires(!tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler, Duration>))       constexpr auto operator()(TimeScheduler&& s, Duration&& d) const noexcept(noexcept( static_cast<TimeScheduler&&>(s).schedule_after((Duration &&) d))) -> _result_t<TimeScheduler, Duration> { return static_cast<TimeScheduler&&>(s).schedule_after((Duration &&) d); } template <typename Duration> constexpr sender<Duration> operator()(Duration d) const { return sender<Duration>{std::move(d)}; } } schedule_after{}; } }
objects.description: Customization-point object for schedule_after. Dispatches to tag_invoke or a scheduler's .schedule_after(). Also acts as a generator of a deferred sender when called with only a duration.

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _schedule_at { inline const struct _fn { private: template <typename TimeScheduler, typename TimePoint> using _schedule_at_member_result_t = decltype(UNIFEX_DECLVAL(TimeScheduler) .schedule_at(UNIFEX_DECLVAL(TimePoint))); template <typename TimeScheduler, typename TimePoint> using _result_t = typename conditional_t< tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler, TimePoint>, meta_tag_invoke_result<_fn>, meta_quote2<_schedule_at_member_result_t>>:: template apply<TimeScheduler, TimePoint>; public: template(typename TimeScheduler, typename TimePoint)         (requires tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler, TimePoint>)       constexpr auto operator()(TimeScheduler&& s, TimePoint&& tp) const noexcept(is_nothrow_tag_invocable_v<_fn, TimeScheduler, TimePoint>) -> _result_t<TimeScheduler, TimePoint> { return tag_invoke(*this, (TimeScheduler &&) s, (TimePoint &&) tp); } template(typename TimeScheduler, typename TimePoint)           (requires(!tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler, TimePoint>))       constexpr auto operator()(TimeScheduler&& s, TimePoint&& tp) const noexcept(noexcept( static_cast<TimeScheduler&&>(s).schedule_at((TimePoint &&) tp))) -> _result_t<TimeScheduler, TimePoint> { return static_cast<TimeScheduler&&>(s).schedule_at((TimePoint &&) tp); } template <typename TimePoint> constexpr sender<TimePoint> operator()(TimePoint tp) const { return sender<TimePoint>{std::move(tp)}; } } schedule_at{}; } }
objects.description: Customization-point object for schedule_at. Dispatches to tag_invoke or a scheduler's .schedule_at(). Also acts as a generator of a deferred sender when called with only a time point.

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _now { inline const struct _fn { private: template <typename TimeScheduler> using _now_member_result_t = decltype(UNIFEX_DECLVAL(TimeScheduler).now()); template <typename TimeScheduler> using _result_t = typename conditional_t< tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler>, meta_tag_invoke_result<_fn>, meta_quote1<_now_member_result_t>>::template apply<TimeScheduler>; public: template(typename TimeScheduler)                  (requires tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler>)       constexpr auto operator()(TimeScheduler&& s) const noexcept(is_nothrow_tag_invocable_v<_fn, TimeScheduler>) -> _result_t<TimeScheduler> { return tag_invoke(*this, (TimeScheduler &&) s); } template(typename TimeScheduler)                    (requires(!tag_invocable<_fn, TimeScheduler>))       constexpr auto operator()(TimeScheduler&& s) const noexcept(noexcept(static_cast<TimeScheduler&&>(s).now())) -> _result_t<TimeScheduler> { return static_cast<TimeScheduler&&>(s).now(); } } now{}; } }
objects.description: Customization-point object for obtaining the current time from a time scheduler. Dispatches to tag_invoke or a scheduler's .now().

objects.definition: namespace unifex { namespace _current { struct _scheduler { #if !UNIFEX_NO_COROUTINES private: template(typename Tag, typename Promise)  (requires same_as<Tag, tag_t<await_transform>> AND scheduler_provider<Promise&>)  friend auto tag_invoke(Tag, Promise& promise, _scheduler) noexcept { return _awaiter{get_scheduler(promise)}; } #endif public: auto schedule() const noexcept { return unifex::schedule(); } template <typename Duration> auto schedule_after(Duration d) const { return unifex::schedule_after(std::move(d)); } template <typename TimePoint> auto schedule_at(TimePoint tp) const { return unifex::schedule_at(std::move(tp)); } friend constexpr bool operator==(_scheduler, _scheduler) noexcept { return true; } friend constexpr bool operator!=(_scheduler, _scheduler) noexcept { return false; } constexpr _scheduler operator()() const noexcept { return {}; } }; } }
objects.description: A trivial scheduler type representing the coroutine's current scheduler. Provides schedule, schedule_after, and schedule_at by forwarding to the unifex CPOs. Supports co_await current_scheduler() to obtain the scheduler from a scheduler_provider promise.

Enumeration of blocking characteristics for a sender/operation. Values indicate whether completion may occur inline, always before return, maybe asynchronously, or never inline (i.e., always asynchronous).

Value wrapper around _enum that provides named integral_constant constants for common blocking kinds and implicit conversion to/from the enum. Used to query and represent a sender's blocking behavior.

Customization-point object type for querying a sender's blocking_kind. It uses tag_invoke if available; otherwise it falls back to checking a Sender::blocking static member or returns blocking_kind::maybe.

Alias brought into unifex namespace via 'using _block::blocking_kind;'. This is not a separate definition; it refers to unifex::_block::blocking_kind. Included here only to note the public name; all details are in unifex::_block::blocking_kind.
Function-object type that, when invoked with an exception object, throws it (or calls std::terminate() if exceptions are disabled). Exposed via the inline constexpr instance unifex::throw_.

Internal lightweight type that holds an address to an exception object and a function pointer capable of rethrowing it. Used only when UNIFEX_HAS_FAST_MAKE_EXCEPTION_PTR == 0 to decouple exception construction from templates. The rethrow() member is declared here and defined out-of-line (not present in this header). Move construction is disabled.

Function-object type that produces a std::exception_ptr from an exception object. In the slow-path configuration (UNIFEX_HAS_FAST_MAKE_EXCEPTION_PTR == 0), it takes a unifex::_except_ptr::_ref and returns a std::exception_ptr via an out-of-line implementation; in the fast-path it forwards to std::make_exception_ptr. Exposed via the inline constexpr instance unifex::make_exception_ptr.

Intrusive task node for the manual event loop. Carries a function pointer used to execute the task and a next pointer to form a singly-linked queue. Constructed with an execute function which will be invoked by execute(). Lifetime/ownership are managed by the event loop queue; details not specified in this header.

Manual event loop that runs a queue of task_base nodes. Provides a scheduler for scheduling no-arg tasks that complete immediately upon execution. run() processes enqueued tasks until stop() is called; enqueue() adds tasks to the queue. Thread-safety is via internal mutex/condition_variable. Aliased publicly as unifex::manual_event_loop.
Scheduler handle associated with a context. Exposes schedule() which returns a sender (schedule_task). Equality compares underlying context pointer. Instances are created by context::get_scheduler().

objects.definition: using manual_event_loop = _manual_event_loop::context;
objects.description: Public alias that exposes _manual_event_loop::context as unifex::manual_event_loop.

Sender type returned by scheduler::schedule() that completes inline. It has no value signals, may send done, and sends std::exception_ptr as error. connect() constructs the corresponding operation state for a given Receiver.

Inline scheduler type whose schedule() returns a sender that completes synchronously on the calling thread. All equality comparisons compare equal. Provides a nested schedule_task sender and a schedule() factory.
A customization point object (CPO) that constructs a just sender from the provided values by forwarding to _just::sender in-place constructor.

Customization point object type for then. Provides callable interface that either dispatches to tag_invoke(_fn, Sender, Func) or constructs the default then-sender with captured return address. A global inline constexpr instance unifex::then is defined as this type.

Helper that establishes an async stack root/frame for tracing during sync_wait. Activates an AsyncStackFrame on construction and deactivates it on destruction. Holds the frame and a ScopedAsyncStackRoot.

Customization point object type for sync_wait. Instances call senders and block, returning an optional of the sender’s single value. The translation unit defines an inline constexpr instance named sync_wait elsewhere in this header.

functions.name: unifex::_tag_invoke::tag_invoke
functions.signature: void tag_invoke();
functions.description: Sentinel declaration used to participate in ADL-based customization for tag_invoke. It is not intended to be called directly and has no definition here; real overloads are provided by libraries/users for specific CPO/argument combinations. Presence of this declaration allows unqualified calls to tag_invoke(cpo, args...) to find user-defined overloads via ADL.
requirements: Do not call this zero-argument declaration; it has no definition and is only a sentinel for ADL participation.
Callers should instead invoke tag_invoke with a customization point object (CPO) and arguments for which a matching overload is provided by the CPO/library or by user code.

functions.name: unifex::_tag_invoke::_fn::operator()
functions.signature:
template <typename CPO, typename... Args>
constexpr auto operator()(CPO cpo, Args&&... args) const noexcept(noexcept(tag_invoke((CPO&&)cpo, (Args&&)args...))) -> decltype(tag_invoke((CPO&&)cpo, (Args&&)args...));
functions.description: Dispatches to an unqualified tag_invoke(cpo, args...) via ADL. This is the callable interface of the tag_invoke CPO: invoking it forwards the given CPO and arguments to the corresponding tag_invoke overload and returns its result. The call is conditionally noexcept if the selected tag_invoke is noexcept.
requirements: CPO and Args... must form a valid call expression tag_invoke((CPO&&)cpo, (Args&&)args...) found by ADL; otherwise the call is ill-formed.
Any preconditions imposed by the selected tag_invoke overload (argument states, lifetimes, ranges, etc.) must be met by the caller.
Exception safety follows the selected tag_invoke overload; this operator is noexcept only if the underlying tag_invoke is noexcept.

functions.name: unifex::set_value
functions.signature:
template <typename Receiver, typename... Values>
(requires tag_invocable<unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_value_fn, Receiver, Values...>)
auto set_value(Receiver&& r, Values&&... values) noexcept(is_nothrow_tag_invocable_v<unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_value_fn, Receiver, Values...>)
  -> decltype(unifex::tag_invoke(unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_value_fn{}, (Receiver&&)r, (Values&&)values...));
functions.description: Customization point object (CPO) to deliver a successful value signal to a receiver. This overload dispatches via tag_invoke if available. Typical usage: unifex::set_value(receiver, values...). It forwards arguments and returns whatever the customization returns.
requirements: Receiver and Values... must form a valid tag_invocable for unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_value_fn.
The tag_invoke(…, Receiver, Values...) must be nothrow-invocable.
No explicit constraints on the return type beyond what tag_invoke provides (may be void or another type as defined by the customization).
Receiver may be cv/ref-qualified; it is forwarded (may be moved).
Values... are perfectly forwarded.

functions.name: unifex::set_next
functions.signature:
template <typename Receiver, typename... Values>
(requires tag_invocable<unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_next_fn, Receiver, Values...>)
auto set_next(Receiver& r, Values&&... values) noexcept(is_nothrow_tag_invocable_v<unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_next_fn, Receiver, Values...>)
  -> decltype(unifex::tag_invoke(unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_next_fn{}, r, (Values&&)values...));
functions.description: Customization point object (CPO) to deliver an intermediate/next value signal to a receiver (typically for sequence/stream receivers). This overload dispatches via tag_invoke if available. Typical usage: unifex::set_next(receiver, values...).
requirements: Receiver is passed by non-const lvalue reference.
Receiver and Values... must form a valid tag_invocable for unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_next_fn.
The tag_invoke(…, Receiver&, Values...) must be nothrow-invocable.
Values... are perfectly forwarded.

functions.name: unifex::set_error
functions.signature:
template <typename Receiver, typename Error>
(requires tag_invocable<unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_error_fn, Receiver, Error>)
auto set_error(Receiver&& r, Error&& error) noexcept
  -> decltype(unifex::tag_invoke(unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_error_fn{}, (Receiver&&)r, (Error&&)error));
functions.description: Customization point object (CPO) to deliver an error signal to a receiver. This overload dispatches via tag_invoke if available. Typical usage: unifex::set_error(receiver, error).
requirements: Receiver and Error must form a valid tag_invocable for unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_error_fn.
The tag_invoke(…, Receiver, Error) must be nothrow-invocable (enforced by static_assert).
The tag_invoke return type must be void (enforced by static_assert).
Receiver may be moved-from by this call if r is an rvalue.
Error is perfectly forwarded.

functions.name: unifex::set_done
functions.signature:
template <typename Receiver>
(requires tag_invocable<unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_done_fn, Receiver>)
auto set_done(Receiver&& r) noexcept
  -> decltype(unifex::tag_invoke(unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_done_fn{}, (Receiver&&)r));
functions.description: Customization point object (CPO) to deliver a done/cancellation signal to a receiver. This overload dispatches via tag_invoke if available. Typical usage: unifex::set_done(receiver).
requirements: Receiver must form a valid tag_invocable for unifex::_rec_cpo::_set_done_fn.
The tag_invoke(…, Receiver) must be nothrow-invocable (enforced by static_assert).
The tag_invoke return type must be void (enforced by static_assert).
Receiver may be moved-from by this call if r is an rvalue.

functions.name: unifex::start
functions.signature: template <typename Operation> requires tag_invocable<unifex::_start_cpo::_fn, Operation&> auto unifex::start(Operation& op) noexcept -> tag_invoke_result_t<unifex::_start_cpo::_fn, Operation&>;
functions.description: Customization point that starts an operation state. If a tag_invoke overload for start is available for Operation&, it is invoked. This call is required to be noexcept and typically returns void. Use when Operation is a valid operation state that provides a start customization via tag_invoke.
requirements: Operation must be an lvalue (Operation&)
A valid tag_invoke(unifex::start, Operation&) overload must exist
The tag_invoke overload must be noexcept (enforced by static_assert)
Return type is tag_invoke_result_t<...> (commonly void)

functions.name: unifex::connect
functions.description: Customization point that connects a sender to a receiver to create an operation state. Prefer tag_invoke(unifex::connect, S, R) if available; otherwise falls back to s.connect(r). When async stack injection is enabled, the returned operation state is wrapped to propagate async stack frames; otherwise, the underlying result is returned. Typical usage: auto op = unifex::connect(std::move(sender), std::move(receiver)); then unifex::start(op).
requirements: S must model unifex::sender
R must model unifex::receiver
Either tag_invoke(unifex::connect, S, R) must be valid, or S must provide a member function connect(R)
Exception specification of unifex::connect follows that of the selected implementation (tag_invoke or member connect, possibly wrapped for async stacks)
Caller must pass arguments suitable for forwarding (S&&, R&&); lifetimes must outlive any created operation state as required by the underlying connect implementation

functions.name: unifex::get_scheduler
functions.description: Returns the current scheduler associated with the given SchedulerProvider by invoking the get_scheduler customization point. Usage: call get_scheduler(provider) where provider has a nothrow tag_invoke overload returning a type that models the unifex::scheduler concept. This is a CPO implemented as a constexpr function object; the signature above reflects its operator().
requirements: SchedulerProvider must have a nothrow customization: tag_invoke(unifex::get_scheduler, const SchedulerProvider&)
The tag_invoke result type must model unifex::scheduler
Argument must be an lvalue (const SchedulerProvider&)

functions.name: unifex::schedule
functions.description: Creates a sender that, when started, completes on the given scheduler (overload taking a Scheduler) or on the receiver’s associated scheduler (nullary overload). The returned sender has value_types = Variant<Tuple<>> (no values), error_types including std::exception_ptr, sends_done = true, blocking_kind = maybe, and is_always_scheduler_affine = true. Use schedule(sched) to reschedule onto a specific scheduler; use schedule() inside an algorithm where the receiver provides a scheduler via get_scheduler.
requirements: For schedule(Scheduler&&): Scheduler must model unifex::scheduler (i.e., be copy-constructible and equality-comparable and provide schedule via tag_invoke or member)
The call to schedule(sched) must be well-formed and may be noexcept depending on the scheduler’s customization
For schedule(): when later connecting the returned sender, the Receiver must be a unifex receiver and get_scheduler(std::as_const(receiver)) must be valid and return a scheduler supporting schedule()

functions.name: unifex::schedule_after
functions.description: Creates a sender that schedules completion after a relative duration. Two forms: (1) schedule_after(sched, dur) uses either tag_invoke or the scheduler’s member function schedule_after to produce a sender. (2) schedule_after(dur) returns a deferred sender that, when connected, fetches the receiver’s associated scheduler via get_scheduler and calls schedule_after(scheduler, dur). Returned senders complete with no values, can send errors (std::exception_ptr), and are scheduler-affine.
requirements: For schedule_after(TimeScheduler, Duration): either tag_invoke(unifex::schedule_after, TimeScheduler, Duration) must be valid, or TimeScheduler must provide a member function schedule_after(Duration)
Exception specification follows the chosen customization (tag_invoke must be nothrow to be nothrow; member call must be noexcept to be nothrow)
For schedule_after(Duration): Duration must be copy-constructible (stored by value inside the sender and passed as const Duration&)
For the deferred sender from schedule_after(Duration): when connecting, get_scheduler(std::as_const(receiver)) must be valid and return a scheduler that supports schedule_after(const Duration&)

functions.name: unifex::schedule_at
functions.description: Creates a sender that schedules completion at an absolute time point. Two forms: (1) schedule_at(sched, tp) uses either tag_invoke or the scheduler’s member function schedule_at to produce a sender. (2) schedule_at(tp) returns a deferred sender that, when connected, fetches the receiver’s associated scheduler via get_scheduler and calls schedule_at(scheduler, tp). Returned senders complete with no values, can send errors (std::exception_ptr), and are scheduler-affine.
requirements: For schedule_at(TimeScheduler, TimePoint): either tag_invoke(unifex::schedule_at, TimeScheduler, TimePoint) must be valid, or TimeScheduler must provide a member function schedule_at(TimePoint)
Exception specification follows the chosen customization (tag_invoke must be nothrow to be nothrow; member call must be noexcept to be nothrow)
For schedule_at(TimePoint): TimePoint must be copy-constructible (stored by value inside the sender and passed as const TimePoint&)
For the deferred sender from schedule_at(TimePoint): when connecting, get_scheduler(std::as_const(receiver)) must be valid and return a scheduler that supports schedule_at(const TimePoint&)

functions.name: unifex::now
functions.description: Retrieves the current time point from a time-aware scheduler. Uses a tag_invoke customization if available; otherwise calls s.now(). Intended for schedulers that support time-based operations such as schedule_after/schedule_at. The exact time point type is scheduler-defined.
requirements: TimeScheduler must either support tag_invoke(unifex::now, TimeScheduler) or provide a member now()
The call is noexcept only if the chosen customization/member is noexcept

functions.name: unifex::current_scheduler
functions.signature: constexpr unifex::_current::_scheduler unifex::current_scheduler() noexcept
functions.description: Returns a stateless scheduler proxy representing the current execution context’s scheduler. The returned object models a scheduler interface with schedule(), schedule_after(Duration), and schedule_at(TimePoint) that produce senders which will execute on the receiver’s current scheduler when connected. In coroutine contexts, co_await current_scheduler() yields the coroutine’s current concrete scheduler if the promise type provides a scheduler (scheduler_provider). Use this to write scheduler-agnostic code that re-schedules work onto the current scheduler.
requirements: Calling current_scheduler() itself has no preconditions and is noexcept.
co_await current_scheduler() requires the awaiting coroutine’s promise type to model scheduler_provider (i.e., get_scheduler(promise) is well-formed and noexcept).
Using the returned object’s schedule_after(Duration) requires that the underlying current scheduler supports schedule_after(Duration) for the provided Duration type.
Using the returned object’s schedule_at(TimePoint) requires that the underlying current scheduler supports schedule_at(TimePoint) for the provided TimePoint type.

functions.name: unifex::blocking
functions.description: Queries the blocking behavior of a Sender via tag_invoke customization. This overload is selected when tag_invoke is available for (unifex::_block::_fn, const Sender&). Typical implementations return a unifex::blocking_kind (or a blocking_kind::constant<...>) describing whether completion is inline, always synchronous, maybe asynchronous, or never synchronous. Use this to inspect a sender’s completion timing characteristics for scheduling/optimization decisions.
requirements: Sender must have a valid tag_invoke overload: tag_invoke(unifex::_block::_fn, const Sender&) must be well-formed.
The tag_invoke implementation should be noexcept if you expect this call to be noexcept; otherwise the noexcept specification depends on is_nothrow_tag_invocable_v.

The returned type is tag_invoke_result_t<...> and is determined by the tag_invoke overload (commonly unifex::blocking_kind or a blocking_kind::constant<...>). Callers must be prepared to handle that exact type.

functions.name: unifex::throw_
functions.signature:
template <typename Exception>
[[noreturn]] void operator()(Exception&& ex) const
functions.description: Function object that unconditionally throws the supplied exception object (or, if exceptions are disabled, calls std::terminate).     std::is_nothrow_invocable_v<unifex::tag_t<unifex::bind_back>, unifex::_then::_cpo::_fn::_impl_fn, Func, instruction_ptr>)

functions.description: Composable sender adaptor. then(predecessor, func) returns a sender that, when the predecessor completes with set_value, invokes func with the predecessor’s value(s). Exceptions thrown by func are caught and delivered to the receiver via set_error(std::exception_ptr) unless func is nothrow-invocable. An overload then(func) returns a pipeable adaptor suitable for use as predecessor | then(func). If a tag_invoke customization for then exists for the given Sender and Func, it is used; otherwise a default _then::sender wrapper is returned.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary string used in several places (exception messages, salts, etc.)
# Fuzzer harness uses:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() -> consumes a blob as a std::string (can include NULs)
# - FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) -> consumes 4 bytes for an unsigned int
# Our goal: craft a single buffer that, when read sequentially by the harness,
# yields interesting combinations:
#  - Various unsigned values to drive branches (e.g., shouldThrow toggles)
#  - Strings of varied sizes (empty, small, medium, large, with NULs and non-ASCII)
#  - Keep within 4096 bytes
# Strategy:
#  - Emit a header with several 32-bit integers deliberately patterned to:
#      * produce both small and large values for value modulo operations
#      * flip LSBs to toggle throw paths
#  - Follow with multiple length-prefixed string segments; many fuzzers treat FUZZ_PARAM_STR
#    as pulling the remainder or a slice; since we cannot know its exact consumption model,
#    we interleave ints and diverse string blocks, so typical parsers that read sequentially
#    will see a good mix. Even if FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads to next NUL, include NULs mid-string.
#  - Include ASCII, UTF-8-like, and binary bytes.
#
# The function generate(seed) -> bytes returns a deterministic (seeded) but varied buffer.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _make_diverse_string(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose chunks: ASCII letters, digits, unicode bytes, NULs, punctuation, repeats
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # Ensure some ASCII
    ascii_pool = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-:/\\,.@#"
    if target_len <= 0:
        return b""
    # Guarantee at least one NUL somewhere for edge-cases
    nul_pos = rng.randrange(target_len) if target_len > 0 else 0
    for i in range(target_len):
        choice = rng.random()
        if i == nul_pos:
            chunks.append(b"\x00")
            continue
        if choice < 0.5:
            chunks.append(bytes([ascii_pool[rng.randrange(len(ascii_pool))]]))
        elif choice < 0.7:
            # UTF-8-ish multibyte start followed by continuation
            lead = rng.choice([0xC2, 0xC3, 0xD0, 0xD1, 0xE2])
            cont = 0x80 | rng.randrange(64)
            chunks.append(bytes([lead, cont]))
        elif choice < 0.85:
            # Binary byte
            chunks.append(bytes([rng.randrange(256)]))
        else:
            # Small run
            b = ascii_pool[rng.randrange(len(ascii_pool))]
            run = 1 + (rng.randrange(3))
            chunks.append(bytes([b]) * run)
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    # Trim to exact length
    return data[:target_len]

def _bounded_len(rng: random.Random, low: int, high: int) -> int:
    # Bias towards small and medium sizes but occasionally large
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.randrange(low, min(high, 64) + 1)
    elif rng.random() < 0.9:
        return rng.randrange(low, min(high, 512) + 1)
    else:
        return rng.randrange(low, high + 1)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    out = bytearray()

    # Header ints to drive various modulo/bit checks in stubs
    # Pattern: small, large, LSB toggles
    header_ints = []
    # value for just() % 1000 etc.
    header_ints.append(rng.randrange(0, 2000))
    # shouldThrow toggle: craft two values, one odd, one even
    base = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 31)
    header_ints.append(base | 1)   # odd -> shouldThrow true
    header_ints.append(base & ~1)  # even -> shouldThrow false
    # Modes for various mod 3/4 dispatches
    header_ints.append(rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFFF))
    header_ints.append(rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFFF))
    header_ints.append(rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFFF))
    header_ints.append(rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFFF))

    for v in header_ints:
        out += _u32(v)

    # Now emit several string blobs; many FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers will take a slice.
    # We'll prefix each blob with its length to help consumers that read length then data,
    # and also concatenate raw data so consumers that just read until exhaustion still see strings.
    string_sections = []
    num_sections = 5 + rng.randrange(0, 4)
    for i in range(num_sections):
        # Choose size ranges; include one empty, one very small, some medium, maybe one larger
        if i == 0:
            slen = 0
        elif i == 1:
            slen = _bounded_len(rng, 1, 16)
        elif i == 2:
            slen = _bounded_len(rng, 8, 128)
        elif i == 3:
            slen = _bounded_len(rng, 64, 1024)
        else:
            slen = _bounded_len(rng, 0, 1500)
        s = _make_diverse_string(rng, slen)
        string_sections.append(s)

    # Assemble with length prefixes (little endian u32) followed by data
    for s in string_sections:
        # Stop if nearing max
        if len(out) + 4 + len(s) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += _u32(len(s))
        out += s

    # Append a final trailer of random bytes to ensure additional entropy for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    remaining = MAX_TOTAL - len(out)
    if remaining > 0:
        trailer_len = min(remaining, 256 + rng.randrange(0, 257))
        trailer = bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(trailer_len))
        out += trailer

    return bytes(out)
